newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller fears gov's race too costly - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller fears gov's race too costly - paper.

text.p: New York State Comptroller Carl McCall, considered one of the leading Democratic challengers in the 1998 gubernatorial race, has openly questioned if he could raise the funds, the New York Times said Monday.

"The basic question has not been answered, which is fund-raising," McCall told the Times in an interview. "That is something that is becoming increasingly difficult, but also increasingly unpleasant: The prospect for raising money when there is little likelihood of reform, I find the current rules distasteful. And the media will focus on it. I don't know that I want to subject myself to that."
The comptroller's concerns fueled longstanding doubts about his willingness to run, the paper said.

The list of other Democrats seen as possible candidates includes: Assembly Majority Leader Michael Bragman, who represents Syracuse, Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, who represents a Manhattan district, New York City Council Speaker Peter Vallone of Queens, Representative Maurice Hinchey of Kingston, and Richard Kahan, the former head of the State Urban Development Corp.

Other members of the party who might consider a bid are Geraldine Ferraro, the former candidate for vice president, though she has talked more about running for the senate, Representative Nita Lowey of Westchester, and Erie County Executive Dennis Gorski, the paper said.
